terms.meaning: Turning one sequence into another, such as a sentence in English into a sentence in German.
The half of the model that reads the input sequence and turns it into a sequence of vectors.
The half of the model that produces the output sequence one token at a time, using the encoder's vectors.
A way to compute an output as a weighted sum of values, where each weight says how well a query matches the matching key.
A score for machine translation that measures overlap with human reference translations. Higher is better.
Several trained models whose predictions are combined. Usually stronger than any single member, and more costly.
Building a tree that shows how a sentence's words group into phrases.
A network that reads a sequence one step at a time, carrying a hidden state from each step to the next.
Long short-term memory: a kind of RNN with gates that help it keep information over many steps.
Attention where queries, keys, and values all come from the same sequence, so each position looks at the others in that sequence.
Several attention operations run side by side on different learned projections, then joined and projected again.
Generating one element at a time, feeding earlier outputs back in as input for the next step.
Adding a layer's input to its output (x + f(x)), which helps deep networks train.
Rescaling each vector so its values have a standard mean and spread, which stabilises training.
The size of the vectors passed between layers. 512 in the base model.
Blocking some attention connections by setting their scores to minus infinity before softmax, so they get zero weight.
The three vectors attention works with. A query is compared to each key; the match scores weight the values.
The paper's attention: softmax of QKᵀ divided by √d_k, multiplied by V.
A function that turns a list of scores into positive weights that add up to 1.
An older attention that scores query-key matches with a small feed-forward network instead of a dot product.
The sizes of the key and value vectors inside one attention head. 64 each in the base model.
Two linear layers with a ReLU between them, applied to each position separately with the same weights.
A learned table that turns each token into a vector.
A vector added to each token's embedding to tell the model where that token sits in the sequence.
The largest number of steps a signal must travel through the network to connect any two positions.
Self-attention limited to a window of r nearby positions, to save compute on long sequences.
A way to split words into frequent sub-word pieces, so rare words can still be represented.
Another sub-word splitting scheme, used here for English-French.
A starting phase where the learning rate rises from small to large before it starts to decay.
Randomly zeroing parts of each sub-layer's output during training, before it is added back to the input.
Training against slightly softened targets instead of a single 100% correct answer.
A measure of how surprised the model is by the correct output. Lower is better.
A decoding method that keeps the best few partial outputs at each step instead of only the single best.
Averaging the weights saved at the last few points in training to get one final model.
Floating-point operations: the paper's estimate of total training compute.
